explanation: Searched Mathlib's integration API for a statement identifying the Lp class of the Bochner integral of an `Lp E 2 μ`-valued curve with the pointwise integral of a jointly strongly measurable representative. Looked at `MeasureTheory/Integral/Prod.lean` (all Fubini lemmas: `integral_prod`, `integral_prod_swap`, `integral_integral`, `integral_integral_swap`, `Integrable.integral_prod_left/right`, `StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_left'`, `integrable_prod_iff'`), `MeasureTheory/Function/AEEqOfIntegral.lean` (`ae_eq_zero_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite`, `ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq_of_sigmaFinite`, `ae_eq_zero_of_forall_inner`, `Lp.ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq`), `MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Unique.lean` (`Lp.ae_eq_of_forall_setIntegral_eq'`), the `Lp` API (`integral_compLp`, `coeFn_compLp`, `L2Space.lean` inner/indicatorConstLp lemmas), `Integral/Bochner/ContinuousLinearMap.lean` (`integral_apply` for CLMs / continuous multilinear maps / `ContinuousMap`), and kernel/composition files (`Integrable.integral_compProd`). Greps for shapes such as `=ᵐ[μ] fun x => ∫ s,`, `∫ s, … : Lp E`, `integral … coeFn …`, `integral_Lp`, `toLp_integral`, `integral_ae_eq` returned nothing matching: Mathlib has the ingredients (Fubini, set-integral characterizations of a.e. equality, the inner-product test lemma) but no declaration stating that the integral of an Lp-valued curve is the Lp class of the pointwise integral, and deriving it from those ingredients requires the substantial argument carried out in the library's proof (integrability of the pointwise integral on finite-measure sets, an inner-product computation with `indicatorConstLp`, Fubini for the restricted product measure, and an orthonormal-basis expansion), so it is neither a duplicate nor a one-step special case.
